questions.question: Explain why the matchstick squares pattern goes 4, 7, 10, 13 and give the next three terms.
questions.expected_answer: The first square needs 4 matches; each new square shares a side, so it adds 3. Next terms: 16, 19, 22.

questions.question: How many matches are needed for 10 squares, and how many squares can be made with 40 matches?
Create a pattern that starts at 3 and doubles. Write five terms and describe the rule.
questions.expected_answer: 3, 6, 12, 24, 48. Start at 3 and multiply each term by 2 to get the next.
